paper.title: Security Context and Authentication Model
paper.context: Use the stated Servlet and thread model. Distinguish an object’s fields, its trust level and the lifetime of its association with the executing thread.

objectives.open-context: Inspect identity, credentials and granted authorities through the Spring Security object model.
objectives.compare-trust: Distinguish absent, unauthenticated, anonymous and verified evidence.
objectives.trace-context-life: Trace holder, context and repository responsibilities across a synchronous request.
objectives.compare-thread-context: Compare thread-local isolation with explicit task-scoped propagation.
objectives.verify-context-cleanup: Validate downstream trust, explicit propagation and cleanup on failure.

questions.prompt: A context object is present at request entry, but getAuthentication() returns null. What can a downstream policy infer from this object?

choices.alpha: A successful provider call has already happened
choices.beta: This context does not supply a current Authentication
choices.delta: The repository has authenticated the request

questions.prompt: Code calls createEmptyContext() and sets a verified Authentication on the returned object. In the default strategy, unrelated code calling getContext() does not see it yet. What explains this?

choices.alpha: The authority list must have more than one entry
choices.beta: The holder reads only persistent sessions
choices.gamma: Creating the object does not associate it with the holder
choices.delta: The context is attached on every principal read

questions.prompt: An authentication filter constructs a token from form input and passes it to the manager. Which distinction matters before using the token for authorization?

choices.alpha: All Authentication implementations represent the same verified state
choices.beta: The manager’s trusted result is distinct from the submitted token
choices.gamma: The URL determines whether the token is trusted
choices.delta: The presence of credentials makes the token verified

questions.prompt: Two configured mechanisms reach the same controller. One returns a UserDetails principal and the other a Jwt. What is an appropriate way to identify the caller?

choices.beta: Read the credentials as the username
choices.gamma: Use the supported name or a deliberate mapping from each accepted principal type
choices.delta: Treat the first granted authority as the username

questions.prompt: The manager returned an accepted token, and getCredentials() is null when an audit event is created. What should the event generator do?

choices.alpha: Record a verified identity and redacted metadata if required
choices.beta: Reject the accepted identity because evidence must remain readable
choices.gamma: Recover the submitted secret for the log
choices.delta: Use the password hash as the principal

questions.prompt: A verified token carries report:read. The endpoint receives a report ID from another team. What remains to be evaluated?

choices.beta: Whether a request field claims the right team
choices.gamma: Only whether the principal name is nonblank
choices.delta: Whether the verified caller may read that stored report

questions.prompt: A support trace shows an AnonymousAuthenticationToken with isAuthenticated() true. A route requires a verified account. Which check addresses the distinction?

choices.beta: Use the framework’s anonymous-aware trust decision
choices.delta: Treat any granted authority as a login result

questions.prompt: A test compares an unauthenticated UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken and a verified result returned by a configured provider. What does the boolean tell the test?

choices.alpha: The first marks proposed evidence and the second records accepted trust in this mechanism
choices.beta: A true boolean universally proves a verified human
choices.gamma: A false boolean proves the caller does not exist
choices.delta: The first token should be used for access because it still has credentials

questions.prompt: A custom authentication component changes the holder during a request. On a later request the context is missing. The configured SecurityContextHolderFilter uses explicit save. Which hypothesis fits?

choices.alpha: Thread-local values should survive any later request
choices.beta: A later MVC mapping erased the password hash
choices.gamma: The updated context was never saved to its configured repository
choices.delta: A larger authority list would persist the context

questions.prompt: A normal pool worker executes a job submitted within a verified Servlet request. The default holder strategy is used. What should the developer assume?

choices.alpha: The worker uses the most recent request context automatically
choices.beta: Propagation has to be explicit if the task needs the request identity
choices.gamma: Every job should switch the application to a global strategy
choices.delta: Authority scope transfers, but the principal does not

questions.prompt: A nested operation temporarily uses a supplied context on a worker that already has a legitimate outer context. Its delegate throws. What should the supported wrapper do?

choices.alpha: Restore the outer context while allowing the failure to propagate
choices.beta: Keep the supplied context for the next task
choices.gamma: Always erase the legitimate outer context

questions.prompt: Write a test plan for a verified user’s report job on a reused worker. Explain how identity is established, how it reaches the worker and what to assert after normal and exceptional returns. Include the anonymous and no-propagation cases.

feedback.alpha: The context can exist before any authentication.
feedback.beta: A container can be present with an empty slot.
feedback.gamma: A placeholder has to be installed separately.
feedback.delta: The context does not establish how the current slot was populated.

empty-container.reason: Check the contained authentication before using the context for a policy decision.

feedback.alpha: Grant count does not associate the object with a thread.
feedback.beta: The holder provides access through its configured execution strategy.
feedback.gamma: A separate setContext call, or equivalent framework operation, is needed.
feedback.delta: A principal read does not update holder state.

active-holder.reason: Distinguish constructing a context from associating it with the execution boundary.

feedback.alpha: The interface has input and result roles.
feedback.beta: The incoming token can carry unverified evidence.
feedback.gamma: A route cannot verify a token by itself.

submitted-evidence.reason: Trace the object returned by the manager and the point where it is associated with the context.

feedback.alpha: The Jwt path violates that assumption.
feedback.beta: Credential material is proof, not an identity API.
feedback.gamma: Choose an identity contract appropriate to the configured mechanisms.
feedback.delta: A grant expresses policy input, not identity.

principal-contract.reason: Check the mechanism’s principal contract at the controller boundary.

feedback.alpha: Credential erasure is compatible with a successful result.
feedback.beta: Security components may erase credentials after verification.
feedback.gamma: Keeping secrets in audit records adds exposure without proving the event.
feedback.delta: A stored verifier is not the caller identity.

erased-proof.reason: Audit outcomes and opaque correlation metadata, never raw proof.

feedback.alpha: The grant alone does not establish stored team ownership.
feedback.beta: A submitted claim is not authoritative team scope.
feedback.gamma: That check is not resource authorization.
feedback.delta: Evaluate the verified scope against application-owned resource data.

permission-scope.reason: Combine request-level authority with the record authorization policy.

feedback.beta: It distinguishes the placeholder from a verified account.
feedback.gamma: Anonymous authentication can have a principal name.

true-placeholder.reason: Use the trust semantics of your configured authorization mechanism.

feedback.alpha: The objects have different provenance and roles here.
feedback.beta: Anonymous Authentication may also return true.
feedback.gamma: It can represent evidence that has not yet been verified.
feedback.delta: Readable proposed proof is not an authorization result.

trusted-construction.reason: Interpret the flag together with provenance and concrete type.

feedback.alpha: Worker reuse is not a persistence contract.
feedback.beta: The symptom concerns context storage, not the original proof.
feedback.gamma: A holder assignment only affects the active execution strategy.
feedback.delta: Grants do not control repository writes.

save-boundary.reason: Check repository save and load separately from request-local association.

feedback.alpha: Default thread-local state does not follow the Runnable.
feedback.beta: The supported wrapper can scope a prepared context to this task.
feedback.gamma: Global state is inappropriate for this boundary.
feedback.delta: The context is thread-bound as a unit.

pool-context.reason: Make a deliberate identity choice for asynchronous work.

feedback.alpha: The wrapper scopes association and restores the prior baseline.
feedback.beta: That extends trust beyond its task.
feedback.gamma: Nested execution should restore previous state.
feedback.delta: Restoring context does not change the delegate’s failure.

exception-restore.reason: Test both empty and pre-existing baselines where nested execution is legal.

worker-review.reason: Require a verified result using anonymous-aware policy at the caller boundary. Decide whether the worker needs that identity and supply the intended context explicitly through a supported wrapper. On an otherwise empty pool worker, an ordinary job should see no caller. A wrapped job observes the selected verified identity only while running. A follow-up task must see the original worker state after successful and exceptional completion. Independently evaluate resource permissions and avoid logging raw credentials.
rubric: Distinguish submitted, anonymous and verified trust.
Explain the holder strategy and explicit propagation.
Check an ordinary job and a wrapped job.
Assert cleanup or restoration after both exit paths.
Separate resource authorization and audit redaction from context propagation.
